record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: For a dispersive billiard table Y, let f_Y(n) denote the number of periodic orbits of the billiard map whose period is at most n. Does the exponential growth rate h = lim_{n→∞} (log f_Y(n))/n exist?

evidence.quote: Let fY (n) be the number of periodic orbits, whose period is less than or equal to n.
Problem 5. Does the limit below exist? h = limn→∞ log fY (n) / n (2.2)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a dispersing (Sinai) billiard table: a compact connected planar region whose boundary $\partial Y$ consists of finitely many smooth curves, each strictly convex when viewed from inside $Y$ (i.e., the boundary has strictly positive curvature with respect to the inward normal). Consider the associated billiard map $T$, defined on the set of unit tangent vectors based on $\partial Y$ pointing into $Y$, which sends a post-collision state to the state immediately after the next collision via the law of equal angles of reflection.

For a positive integer $n$, let $f_Y(n)$ denote the number of periodic orbits of $T$ whose minimal period is at most $n$.

Question: Does the limit
$$h \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log f_Y(n)}{n}$$
exist (as a finite real number)?
artifact.status_search_result: For dispersing billiards, upper exponential bounds on the number of periodic orbits (Stoyanov, Burago–Ferleger–Kononenko) and lower bounds via Markov coding (Chernov) are known, and topological entropy is finite, but the existence of the limit (rather than only $\limsup$) defining the exponential growth rate of periodic orbits does not appear to have been established. Recent works on Sinai billiards (e.g., Baladi–Demers, Demers' ICM survey 2022) discuss measures of maximal entropy and growth of periodic orbits but do not announce a proof of the limit.

status_evidence.title: Topological Entropy and Pressure for Finite Horizon Sinai Billiards (Demers)
status_evidence.snippet: Chernov ... used this to obtain a lower bound on the growth of periodic orbits ... whether the set sees the full topological entropy of the system was left open.
status_evidence.claim: Growth rate of periodic orbits in Sinai billiards is only partially understood; exact asymptotics/limit existence is not established.

status_evidence.title: An estimate from above of the number of periodic orbits for semi-dispersed billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Estimate from above on the number of periodic orbits in semi-dispersing billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Only an upper exponential bound is provided, not the existence of the limit.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Billiards and Statistical Physics (Chernov–Dolgopyat)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of dispersing billiards including periodic orbit and entropy questions.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of the exponential growth limit for periodic orbits of dispersing billiards is not stated as a theorem.
